svg.title: macOS · Shape-mation · builder · Apply filters · 760×680
svg.desc: Mirrors App/Shapemation/ShapemationFiltersView.swift — the builder's first step, Apply filters, REDRAWN 2026-09-21 for round two (code first, Steven's notes on the 2026-09-20 build): the tags are the tag editor's chips (components/tag-suggestions: 33 pt, rx 16.5, black 7 % with a 14-pt label at 75 % and the count in 13-pt secondary), wrapped by ShapemationFlowLayout and sorted by volume, the biggest first; the applied ones sit under APPLIED in accent with their count and an xmark, beside Clear tags; then the ASPECT card (All · Landscape · Portrait · Square segmented, 362×24, and the line '1 landscape · 83 portrait · 0 square — a mixed-orientation set pays cover-fit crop on every photo of the minority.'), the POSITION card ('where the shape's centre lies': Left 0 · Centre 81 · Right 3 column buttons over the 3×3 cells 0 0 0 / 0 76 3 / 0 5 0, a lit column tinting its cells), the live count '164 photo projects' and the contact sheet of the survivors (84 pt tiles, five to a row, the photo cover-fitted into the set's own aspect over black, the shape box in amber) — stacked in one column at 560 pt (two columns from 700). Geometry from the Debug build's accessibility dump on the tram clone (LL_SHAPEMATION=build LL_CHIPS=tram, 2026-09-21): the intro (14 pt, two lines), the 33-pt search field, the cards at 16 pt gaps, rows 41 pt apart; the step scrolls inside the sheet (its own legacy scroller at x 542, the knob 150 of 547) above the pinned 80-pt bar with Next · shape (149×47). The sheet is 560 wide and 680 tall from 32 pt under the window's top edge, overhanging the 680 window as its siblings do. Photos are flat stand-ins.

g.text: What do you want to make?
Hours become seconds, motion melts into streaks
Interval photos into a timelapse, or one long exposure
Speed rises or falls across the clip
Narrow the photos before choosing the shape — the way the Gallery's Tags
